correctness.rationale: The radial restriction establishes nonnegative F and identifies harmonic lines with zeros. D’Angelo Theorem 1 matches exactly and gives global logarithmic plurisubharmonicity, not just away from zeros. Jensen gives total Riesz mass <=m from growth, smooth nonnegative quadratic vanishing assigns >=1 unit per zero, and equality uniquely enforces the harmonic Liouville remainder and modulus-square factorization. Homogenization is valid in a chart whose infinity is nonzero; product examples attain the exact bound.

value.rationale: A direct finite-direction sharpness theorem for a geometrically natural class in the 2026 harmonic-slice rigidity context. Quantifies previously qualitative exceptional-line finiteness with a sharp degree law and completely characterizes saturation, providing an exact finite testing threshold rather than an arbitrary coefficient computation; useful to distinguish maximal degeneracy in plurisubharmonic homogeneous model terms.
